title: VP of Marketing

role_match.role_rationale_from_stage3: Leading a $8.77B graphics division competing directly with 3M requires aggressive market positioning around proven performance claims that resonate with sign manufacturers, wrap installers, and architects. The VP of Marketing owns competitive messaging, brand differentiation, and customer acquisition in segments where Tedlar's documented 60+ year track record and graffiti resistance create powerful proof points. This role cares about: (1) substantiating outdoor durability claims with third-party validated data that withstands competitive scrutiny at ISA and FESPA events, (2) addressing customer churn caused by premature fading/cracking complaints that damage brand reputation in the wrap installer community, (3) creating premium tier messaging for architectural and transit segments where Avery Dennison currently loses deals to specialty PVF-based solutions. Strategic opportunity: Co-marketing partnership where Tedlar's heritage brand (60+ years) validates Avery Dennison's premium positioning, enabling joint case studies from the DPD fleet project and architectural installations that demonstrate superior graffiti cleaning and zero-yellowing performance. This directly supports marketing's need to win high-visibility municipal and corporate accounts where specification documents increasingly require 15-20 year performance warranties that exceed current product capabilities.

engagement_strategy.scope_and_authority: As VP of Marketing for a $8.77B graphics division, [Name] owns competitive positioning, brand messaging, and market differentiation strategy across all customer segments (sign manufacturers, wrap installers, architectural specifiers, fleet managers). They oversee go-to-market campaigns for product launches, manage messaging at major trade shows (ISA, FESPA), and drive customer acquisition in premium segments. They report to C-suite leadership and influence product development roadmap through customer feedback and competitive intelligence. Marketing likely manages relationships with key accounts like the 30,000-vehicle DPD fleet project and shapes warranty positioning that sales teams use to compete against 3M and specialty film providers.
engagement_strategy.relevant_use_cases: Tedlar's graffiti resistance and UV protection directly address two marketing pain points: (1) Architectural and transit wraps where vandalism requires costly replacement—Tedlar's spray paint/marker cleaning capability becomes a differentiated selling point for municipal contracts and high-traffic building facades. (2) Premium fleet graphics (like the DPD project) where brand reputation depends on graphics maintaining color vibrancy beyond the current 5-12 year lifespan—Tedlar's 12-20+ year outdoor performance without fading or cracking enables superior warranty claims. For marketing, this translates to defensible competitive messaging: documented performance data that withstands scrutiny at trade shows where Avery Dennison faces 3M head-to-head, and proof points for premium tier positioning in architectural and transit segments where current products reach performance limits.
engagement_strategy.personal_stakes: [Name] likely owns metrics around: brand perception scores in the wrap installer community, win rates against 3M in premium architectural/transit bids, customer retention rates (impacted by premature product failure complaints), and market share growth in high-specification segments. Their performance depends on creating messaging that justifies premium pricing while reducing customer churn from quality issues. Tedlar addresses both: (1) Graffiti resistance and extreme temperature range (-70°F to 230°F) provide concrete proof points that differentiate from 3M Scotchcal in RFP responses for municipal transit and building wraps, and (2) Third-party validated outdoor performance data (60+ years of field history) gives marketing defensible claims that reduce warranty-related reputation damage when installers experience fading or cracking with current films.
engagement_strategy.timing_factors: Avery Dennison exhibited at ISA International Sign Expo 2025 in April, celebrating 90 years of vinyl graphic films—making NOW the post-show period where marketing evaluates competitive landscape and customer feedback to refine positioning. The company's recent completion of the massive DPD fleet wrap (30,000 vehicles, 4,500 trailers over three years) creates urgency around performance validation: if those wraps begin showing UV degradation or vandalism issues within the claimed 5-12 year window, marketing faces reputation risk. Additionally, Avery Dennison's active FESPA presence alongside HP, Epson, and 3M means [Name] is continuously benchmarking competitive claims—a Tedlar partnership or technology integration could be positioned as a strategic response to market demands for proven 15-20 year warranties that current cast vinyl technology cannot reliably deliver.

personalization_hooks.hook: Avery Dennison's Supreme Wrapping Film claims 5-12 year outdoor life, but architectural and transit RFPs increasingly require 15-20 year performance specifications
personalization_hooks.messaging_angle: Open conversation around the performance gap between current cast vinyl capabilities and emerging customer requirements in municipal and corporate segments—position Tedlar as enabling a documented solution to this specification challenge rather than a competitive threat

personalization_hooks.hook: The 30,000-vehicle DPD fleet project represents significant brand exposure where any premature fading, cracking, or graffiti damage directly impacts Avery Dennison's reputation with enterprise accounts
personalization_hooks.messaging_angle: Reference the DPD project as a proof point of Avery Dennison's market leadership, then frame Tedlar's graffiti cleaning and UV resistance as protective insurance for high-visibility installations—suggest exploring how Tedlar could enhance warranty confidence for future mega-projects

personalization_hooks.hook: Recent ISA Sign Expo 2025 participation celebrating 90 years of heritage, but facing head-to-head competition with 3M in the premium segment
personalization_hooks.messaging_angle: Acknowledge Avery Dennison's industry legacy, then position Tedlar (with its own 60+ year track record) as a strategic differentiator—suggest a co-marketing approach where combining heritage brands creates unmatched credibility for ultra-premium architectural and transit applications

recommended_approach: Lead with competitive differentiation and market opportunity rather than product specs. Frame Tedlar as a strategic partner that enhances Avery Dennison's premium positioning, not a replacement for their existing technology. Focus on the business case: how documented 15-20 year performance enables marketing to win bids in high-specification architectural/transit segments where current products face limitations, and how graffiti resistance addresses a real customer pain point in municipal contracts. Use the DPD fleet project and ISA presence as evidence of market leadership, then position Tedlar as the missing piece that extends that leadership into ultra-premium tiers.
